title.value: Screening methods for congenital anomalies in low and lower-middle income countries: A systematic review
title.justification: The main focus of the paper is on reviewing screening methods for congenital anomalies in low and lower-middle income countries, as stated in the title and reinforced by the content of the paper.
title.quote: This study aims to identify feasible screening methods for surgically correctable congenital anomalies in LMICs.

extractions.description: This paper is a systematic review examining the various prenatal and neonatal screening methods used to detect surgically correctable congenital anomalies in low and lower-middle income countries (LMICs). It emphasizes the necessity for early detection of these anomalies to reduce morbidity and mortality rates in affected children in LMICs. The paper identifies existing screening methods, evaluates their feasibility, and discusses their risks and limitations, highlighting the need for further research and development of cost-effective, low-resource settings-appropriate screening techniques.

sustainable_development_is_central.justification: The paper primarily focuses on medical and healthcare aspects, specifically improving screening methods for congenital anomalies in LMICs. While important for healthcare and development, this theme is not directly related to Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development.
sustainable_development_is_central.quote: Early identification through fetal and neonatal screening is critical to reducing death and disability. This study aims to identify feasible screening methods for surgically correctable congenital anomalies in LMICs.
